The gates job reruns on the verdict commit, which changes only verify/verification-contract/; its result is read before the verdict is posted on the PR.

observations: npm ci in verdict.yml (builder choice 1): accepted. The outputs do not list the workflow, but the outcome says the verdict gate runs the named tests at the head, and in CI any named test that imports a workspace (xstate, the engine) cannot run without the install. The job already runs the head's own scripts, so the step adds no trust it did not have, and permissions stay contents: read. plan-and-suite-pass is MET on that reading; the done replan's decision file should add verdict.yml to the record.

done_on left out of the frozen contract (builder choice 3): accepted, and needed. Without it every done replan of a fix item would be refused, since the verdict file exists by then. The side effect: any PR may now change done_on at any time, label or not, and done_on feeds the fix budget's 14-day window; check.mjs checks only its format. A later item could freeze done_on once set (allow only absent to a date).

The gate runs each named file as the entry point, not with node --test <file> as decision 2 says. Confirmed: under --test a name pattern matching nothing reports 1 test, 1 pass; as the entry point it reports 0, so the gate can refuse it. docs/gates.md states the real command; the decision text now differs and the done replan should say so.

The verdict-file cutoff sees only the PR's base and head. While the verdict lives on the build branch, a replan PR from main cannot see it, so it may still reword a doing item's Expect checks after verification started. Merging main back into the build branch does not invalidate the verdict either (the replan commit is behind the new merge-base), so the gate would then check the old verdict against the reworded head; only an added or removed Expect id is caught. Worth a line in verify-evidence-policy or a small follow-up (for example, compare the item head at verified_sha with the head).
